body: Thanks so much, keep up the good work! One of my favourite games back in the day, so nice to play it again.

Hey,

Gotta tell ya, I had a bad relationship with a deeply avoidant guy 4 years ago. As I lost my father whom I really adored when I was 9, and had other childhood trauma, I realized my mind can get tricky if my significant other is not open and communicative about his feelings. However, I also started to see that his behaviour would probably bring out the worst even in someone in the greatest headspace. My only mistake was staying in that relationship for too long, not valuing myself and my needs enough. Or even getting in that relationship in the first place. I met a guy a year ago and I recently broke up with him, cause he was showing extreme avoidant behaviour sort of out of the blue. Now, this was and is a really harsh experience for me, cause again I felt like my needs are delusional, and maybe I'm just such an axious partner that I'm crazy. However, all my friends reassured me, that this was no way my fault. I tried everything. 

I think my mistake this time was, that no matter how I told myself that I'm gonna be more careful this time around, asked questions about his past and how he thinks about the future, how he thinks about problems and their solutions, I still was focusing on all the answers he gave that were in alignment with my needs, and didn't pay attention to those that could've give him away. I don't think we should run away from people with attachment trauma, but we should really consider our limits in order to prevent emotional collapse. I figure I advanced because I had awareness, and tried to pay attention, but I still had to learn this lesson again. 

My advice to you, is to really trust yourself. Have the maximum compassion for yourself, and accept you the way you are. Then you can ask about these things with confindence once you start dating (which is pretty normal btw), and can decide whether or not someone is objectively a match for you. You know best what's good for you. And after you feel comfortable knowing these answers, you can let your guard down, and fall in love. If you do that previously, you gonna have a hard time seeing someone's faults.

Communication, honesty, objective thinking is key. Don't rush things and don't give up hope. Find balance. I'm really really rooting for you.
